root_idea.summary: The root centers on interpenetration and close joining, exemplified by flesh as interwoven bodily tissue.
root_idea.development: From this image of intermingled flesh, usage extends to joining, knitting, woven structures, cohesive bonds, wounds becoming covered with flesh, and the battlefield as a place of intermingling. Other branches concern flesh as food, prey, or material for animals.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular noun citation form لَحْمٌ.

senses.definition: Flesh or meat: the fleshy bodily substance, especially as an edible part of humans or animals.
senses.usage_conditions: Used literally for flesh or meat, including flesh mentioned as food, bodily substance, or provision. The Quranic plural لُحُومُ is included under this citation form.

senses.definition: In the image of eating a dead brother’s flesh, the flesh represents backbiting, vilification, or injurious talk about an absent person.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-specific figurative construction in which eating flesh is used as an image for backbiting and defamation; it remains an extended use of the noun rather than a separate physical kind of flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleshy or corpulent; having abundant flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective for a person or other being characterized by substantial flesh; related forms describe possession of flesh and fat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fond of meat or accustomed to eating meat; meat-eating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or, by extension, to an animal such as a falcon or wolf that habitually eats flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A house or place in which meat is available.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression describing a place characterized by having meat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed someone or an animal meat; to provide a bird with flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction with the recipient or animal as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One supplied with meat or hunted prey; by extension, one associated with furnishing or being furnished with meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The classical description applies especially to prey allotted from a hunt and may also describe one supplied from another source; the form is related to the act of feeding with meat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment in which the warp and weft are interwoven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A textile designation based on the interpenetration of its threads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The woof: the threads woven across and into the warp of a cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A textile term for the cross-threads or weft of woven fabric; the related vocalization لُحْمَةٌ is also attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bond of affiliation, kinship, or social connection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively in the expression comparing a legal or social bond to the bond of lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To join, mend, or fit two things together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes making things adhere or restoring their connection, by analogy with flesh joining bones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Material used to join or mend a vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for what effects a repair or union between parts of a container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strip or remove meat from a bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction with the meat as the object removed from the bone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close a hole with a patch; to consolidate or close a wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a garment, piece of cloth, skin, or hide, and of the consolidation of wounds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kill someone, making him prey or meat for wild animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative causative construction presenting the slain person as meat for beasts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone the opportunity or power to revile, vilify, or censure another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form IV construction in which another person’s honor or reputation is made available as an object of verbal attack.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become joined or knit together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI intransitive or reciprocal construction describing things becoming connected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To coalesce, consolidate, close up, or become closely united.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII construction emphasizing the resulting close union or consolidation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleshy substance or pulp, including the substantial flesh of a fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression describing dates as having flesh or substantial pulp.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The portion of quarry or meat given to a falcon after it hunts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression for a bird’s allotted share of its catch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slain person, conceived as having been made into meat for beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative designation derived from treating the dead as prey or food for wild animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A battle or bloody melee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is associated with the intermingling of combatants and with the bodies of the slain lying like scattered flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The narrow or fleshy parts of the female pudendum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical plural expression; the singular is described as مَلْحَمَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The tunica albuginea, or white outer membrane of the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term in later usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A head wound that has become covered with flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a wound whose damaged area has acquired or been covered by flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a crop, having wheat formed in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare agricultural usage describing the formation of wheat within the crop.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tightly twisted rope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive usage based on the close interlocking of the rope’s strands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A butcher.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional designation.

cautions: The classical description of مُلْحِمٌ permits both association with supplying meat and with being supplied with prey, depending on construction; it is therefore kept distinct from the clearly defined Form IV feeding action.
